findings.text: assert LARGE_PATH in definition["write_paths"] is not independent of the value under test: line 332 builds the node with write_paths=[LARGE_PATH] as well as regenerate_paths=[LARGE_PATH], so the assertion holds even if the __post_init__ fold at reckon/crew/node.py:766 is deleted, and it therefore cannot guard the 'a regenerated path is folded into the write scope' claim its own docstring makes. The fold is guarded elsewhere -- the census tests and the scope-conflict test both fail without it -- so this is a misleading assertion rather than an unguarded behaviour.

The module-level REFERENCE_TOKENS = routing._REGENERATED_PATH_REFERENCE_TOKENS makes the base arm a collection error rather than a set of failing tests: logs/gate-base.log reads 1 error, 0 failure ids, EXIT=2, so the base arm shows only that the constant is absent and cannot distinguish a missing option from a wrong one. The done-when asks that the tests fail there; the semantic falsification is carried by the negative-control log (2 failed, EXIT=1) instead, so the base arm is weaker evidence than the done-when describes.

The done-when requires that the live pointer and the promoted ledger row carry the regenerated paths; the file asserts the live pointer (as_dict and crew.pointer_path) but no assertion anywhere names a promoted ledger row, so the ledger half of that measure is implemented (reckon/crew/promotion.py:1911 copies record['node'], which reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2134 fills from node.as_dict()) and unverified. The rebuilt-from-run-directory fallback at reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:134 replaces node with {'write_paths': declared} and so drops regenerate_paths, which no reader currently depends on.
